title: Perran and the Flying Ribbon
markdown:
The sun found Perran’s stable window and painted the stall gold. He blinked, a fizzy feeling already practising in his chest. Today had a different temperature, as if the morning had put on extra shine.

Dot the chimney swift landed on his nose, charcoal feathers catching the light. “Morning, Perran. The air is buzzing. The sky is almost singing.”

He twitched his long ears. “Zippy. Like a race about to start.”

A playful wind snatched a long bright pink ribbon from Mrs. Gable’s washing line next door. It danced and twirled, a magnificent streak against brilliant blue, a streamer waving hello to the whole field.

“Look at that zoom. Where is it going?”

“Follow it. Follow it.” Dot became a tiny black arrow, barely visible against the canvas. Perran did not need a second invitation. He galloped the dewy meadow, powerful legs pumping, hooves a happy piston-song. The ribbon seemed to giggle and swish, leading them toward the big red brick school at the edge of town. It dipped and bobbed, a playful invitation to a grand chase. Once it nearly hooked a hawthorn and thought better of it. Once it looped as if writing a letter in air.

Up it spun, and sat on the flat sunny roof. Perran trotted to the schoolyard edge and stretched his neck. “Stuck. How do we get it down?”

Dot circled the pink, then dropped to his mane like a feather. “We’ll figure it out. But Perran. This roof is a bit like my home, up high. The best part of being a swift is we spend almost our whole lives flying. We eat up here. We drink up here. We can even sleep while we glide.”

Perran’s mouth opened. “Sleep? While flying?” He pictured clouds as a mattress, no ground required. The thought was so large it made the ribbon look suddenly small.

Dot’s laugh was wind-chimes. “We tuck our wings and let the breeze carry us. Like this ribbon.”

The pink fluttered from the chimney, as if nodding. Perran looked at it, at Dot’s silhouette, at the boundless sky. A world of eating and drinking and sleeping in air. He stretched his neck to feel the wind the way she did, not to grab, only to know.

The ribbon snagged securely on the tall chimney. Destination reached. Strangely, the prize had changed. The ribbon was still pretty. The idea was prettier: living with wings, or legs, open.

They did not declare the day amazing. Perran tossed his mane. The sun felt warmer for having been explained. He and Dot turned from the school roof, a neigh and a chirp, and took the meadow path without the pink. Behind them it kept waving, a leftover hello, while the sky went on being a place you could, if you were a swift, sleep in.
